title: See How Great a Flame Aspires
description: See How Great a Flame Aspires in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 306 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Progress of the Gospel”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: See how great a flame as-pires, Kin-dled by a spark of grace! Je-sus' love the na-tions fires, Sets the king-doms on a blaze. To bring fire on earth he came: Kin-dled in some hearts it is: O that all might catch the flame, All par-take the glo-rious bliss!

lines: See how great a flame aspires,
Kindled by a spark of grace!
Jesus' love the nations fires,
Sets the kingdoms on a blaze.
To bring fire on earth he came:
Kindled in some hearts it is:
O that all might catch the flame,
All partake the glorious bliss!
When he first the work begun,
Small and feeble was his day:
Now the word doth swiftly run,
Now it wins its widening way:
More and more it spreads and grows,
Ever mighty to prevail;
Sin's strong-holds it now o'erthrows,
Shakes the trembling gates of hell.
Saw ye not the cloud arise,
Little as a human hand?
Now it spreads along the skies,
Hangs o'er all the thirsty land!
Lo! the promise of a shower
Drops already from above!
Haste, O Lord, and quickly pour
All the spirit of thy love.

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
